newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay preferred as new Thai PM - poll.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay preferred as new Thai PM - poll.

text.p: Thai Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan emerged as the favourite choice for the post of Prime Minister in a spot survey conducted by the Bangkok Post.
The results of the informal survey were published on Tuesday.

It showed that 47 percent of the 121 local and foreign businessmen and government officials polled would choose Amnuay as prime minister to replace Banharn Silpa-archa, who announced his resignation at the weekend.
At present, Amnuay is also deputy prime minister and in charge of all economic matters.

Former Prime Minister Chuan Leekpai, who heads the opposition Democrat Party, received the second-biggest number of votes with 33 percent, while Defence Minister and New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh -- considered the front runner for the position -- won four percent of support.
About 62 percent of those surveyed also felt parliament should be dissolved if the six coalition partners were unable to agree on the formation of a new government.

Banharn announced on Saturday that he would step down within seven days after finding a suitable successor. His resignation came after three days of a bruising no-confidence debate against him in parliament.

Political analysts say Banharn, who was forced to resign after several coalition partners threatened to withdraw support for him in the censure vote, may decide to dissolve parliament if a suitable candidate for premier cannot be agreed upon by the coalition.
